10.title: Electrification Caucus Co-Chairs Call For Action On Household Electrification Measures
10.description:
Electrification Caucus Co-Chairs U.S. Representatives Kathy Castor (D-Fla.), Chair of the House Select Committee on the Climate Crisis, and Paul Tonko (D-N.Y.) and U.S. Senators Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.) and Tina Smith (D-Minn.) will host a virtual briefing on Wednesday, February 16 at 4 p.m. ET to discuss why Congress must make progress to advance policies to accelerate widespread electrification, including making household electrification easy and affordable through consumer rebates. 

Electrifying homes, commercial buildings, and vehicles has broad support and is one of the most practical actions we can take to address the climate crisis, lower costs for American families, create jobs, and improve indoor air quality.

The Electrification Caucus Co-Chairs will be joined by Mayor of Houston Sylvester Turner, CEO of Rewiring America Ari Matusiak, and CEO of Redfin Glenn Kelman.

18.title: Briefing on the IPCC’s 6th Assessment Report
18.description:
At 1:00 p.m. on Wednesday, September 1st, 2021, the House Select Committee on the Climate Crisis will hold a briefing on the IPCC's dire August 2021 report highlighting how human activity has led to “unprecedented” changes to the Earth’s climate, and warning that – without deep, rapid reductions in greenhouse gas emissions – “warming of 1.5°C and 2°C will be exceeded during the 21st century.”

More information is available at: https://climatecrisis.house.gov/committee-activity/other-activities/briefing-ipcc-s-6th-assessment-report

19.title: Financing Climate Solutions and Job Creation
19.description:
The hearing will focus on how Congress can create financial incentives and make smart investments to help families afford clean energy and energy efficiency technologies, to accelerate the deployment of zero-emission cars and trucks, and to create good-paying jobs across America. These incentives and investments include clean energy tax credits; clean vehicle tax credits; tax credits for domestic manufacturing; and a clean energy and sustainability accelerator, which can help support state-level green banks.

Ms. Beth Soholt, Executive Director, Clean Grid Alliance, on behalf of American Council on Renewable Energy and Americans for a Clean Energy Grid

Mr. Michael Shellenberger, Founder & President, Environmental Progress

50.title: Generation Climate: Young Leaders Urge Climate Action Now (720p)
50.description:
Note: This is a higher-quality recording of the hearing.

The House Select Committee on the Climate Crisis will hold its first hearing on Thursday, April 4th. In contrast to a typical Congressional hearing, the committee will hear from young leaders who are urging policymakers to take climate action now and finally address the climate crisis.

“This is the first generation to grow up seeing the effects of the climate crisis in their own backyards. Now they’re demanding the opportunity to solve it. Climate change creates generational scale injustices. It’s a daunting challenge, but this generation is ready to meet it.” - Rep. Kathy Castor

The committee will receive testimony from:

Aji Piper
Plaintiff, Juliana v. United States
Seattle, WA

Chris J. Suggs
Student and activist
Kinston, NC

Melody Zhang
Climate Justice Campaign Coordinator, Sojourners
Co-Chair, Young Evangelicals for Climate Action

Additional witnesses may be added. More information about the hearing, including a live webcast, will be added to this page: https://climatecrisis.house.gov/committee-activity/hearings/generation-climate-young-leaders-urge-climate-action-now
